## About This Project
In this project, you will be responsible for evaluating the quality of localized visual content, specifically videos and images. Your evaluation will primarily involve comparing the source and target assets, focusing on aspects such as Translation, Text Extraction, In-Painting, Rendering, and Text Group Tracking.
The primary objective is to verify that the localized content accurately preserves the original meaning, commercial intent, visual style, and formatting, while effectively communicating the message to the target audience in their language.
## What You Will Do
- Review the provided content and complete evaluations in accordance with the project guidelines.
- Apply annotation standards consistently to ensure high-quality and accurate results.
- Use OneForma’s task tools effectively to complete assigned work correctly and efficiently.
- Adhere to quality, productivity, and compliance requirements throughout task execution.
- Identify, label, and document findings with clear and accurate reasoning when required. Escalate unclear cases or guideline-related questions when necessary.
## Requirements
- Native in the Target language.
- Proficient in the Source language, with the ability to accurately interpret content and assess linguistic issues.
- Detail-oriented and comfortable with linguistic and stylistic evaluation tasks as well as the technical aspect of this evaluation (synchronicity mainly).
- Basic understanding of transcription formats and media content review processes.
- Ability to understand and consistently apply complex client guidelines.
- Prior experience in transcription QA, subtitling, captioning, media localization, or related linguistic quality assurance projects is preferred.
## Language Pairs
Each pair runs from the source language into the target language. Apply for a pair whose target language is your native language.
- Swedish (Sweden) to English (United Kingdom)
- German (Germany) to Polish (Poland)
- German (Germany) to Danish (Denmark)
- German (Germany) to Czech (Czech Republic)
- French (France) to English (United Kingdom)

- Spanish (Spain) to English (United Kingdom)
- Spanish (Spain) to Portuguese (Portugal)
- Japanese (Japan) to English (United States)

Paid per hour, in USD. The rate depends on the language pair.

- Location: Remote. The three Norwegian (Bokmal) pairs are open to residents of Norway only.

## About This Project
Centaurus is a paid video research study. Using your own phone, you record a handful of short, selfie-style videos at home by following simple step-by-step instructions. The whole task takes under 10 minutes.
Open to adults 18+ recording themselves, and to children aged 5 to 17 recorded at home with a parent or guardian present. No prior experience required.
## Why This Work Matters
Your videos support technology research, helping technology better understand real people, real faces, and everyday environments across different ages and settings. The more varied the people and places, the better that technology works for everyone.
Participation is voluntary, and you can withdraw at any time.
## What You’ll Record
- 2 videos indoors: natural, everyday settings
- 2 videos outdoors: regular environments around you
Each clip is about 15 seconds long. You’ll receive clear, guided instructions before you start.
## Recording For A Child
Children aged 5 to 17 can take part too. A parent or guardian sets up the recording, stays present throughout, and provides consent before the child participates. The steps are exactly the same: you simply record your child instead of yourself, following the same simple guide.

- Apply: confirm your eligibility through the form below

Use your medical expertise to review clinical reasoning tasks based on de-identified longitudinal health records. This remote project is open to qualified professionals residing in the United States.
## Description
We are looking for physicians with strong clinical reasoning skills to support a specialized AI-related project involving the review of clinical tasks created from sample, de-identified longitudinal electronic health record (EHR) data.
As a reviewer, you will carefully examine clinical vignettes and their supporting records to assess medical accuracy, completeness, and quality of clinical reasoning. This is not a rapid labeling task: the project requires thoughtful review, attention to detail, and clear clinical justification for your assessments.
All work is completed remotely through OneForma’s secure annotation platform. No connection to an external EHR system is required.
### What you’ll do
For each assigned case, you may be asked to:
- Review a clinical vignette against the supporting de-identified EHR record.
- Identify inaccurate, unsupported, or missing clinical information.
- Assess whether the proposed answer is medically correct, sufficiently specific, and suitable for evaluation.
- Determine whether an alternative answer represents a reasonable but incorrect clinical choice.
- Review the clinical reasoning for logical gaps, contradictions, or unsupported conclusions.
- Document your findings, level of confidence, and clear clinical justification.
- Flag cases that may require review by another specialty or senior adjudication.
- Participate in an initial calibration process before completing reviews independently.
### Who we’re looking for
This project is intended for physicians and medical domain experts who can demonstrate strong clinical judgment and carefully evaluate complex medical information.
To participate, you must:
- Have physician-level medical expertise.
- Be comfortable reviewing longitudinal clinical records and clinical reasoning.
- Be able to provide clear, evidence-based justification for your assessments.
- Have strong attention to detail and be comfortable working independently.
- Be proficient in English (United States).
- Currently reside in the United States.
